today.look_for: Sign-up as it ships: three fields (display name, email, password) under Apple and Google, a disabled Create account, and the sign-in fork as a link at the bottom — Welcome and Sign in are its mirrors.

directions.name: One door
directions.look_for: One screen replaces Welcome’s fork and both forms: Apple, Google, one email field and Continue; the dashed block shows what appears after Continue for a returning address, the caption what a new one gets.

directions.name: Code, not password
directions.look_for: After the email, a six-box one-time-code field with iOS Security Code AutoFill offering the code above the keypad; “Use password instead” and a cooling-down Resend sit under Continue.

directions.name: Two screens, two fields
directions.look_for: The same sign-up screen minus the display-name field: email plus a password iOS has just suggested (“Use Strong Password” in the QuickType bar), Create account already live.

today.look_for: The request form as it ships: the email field is empty even though sign-in just held the address, the button is disabled until it is retyped, and the only way back is the link.

directions.name: Reset lands you inside
directions.look_for: The address is already in the field and Send is live; the dashed block is the sent state with the new Open Mail button, and its last line is the point — setting the password signs you in.

directions.name: Sign in with a code instead
directions.look_for: “Forgot password?” has become “Email me a sign-in code”: the locked-out path is a six-box code screen, and changing the password moves to a row under Profile → Account (dashed block).

directions.name: Passkey after first sign-in
directions.look_for: A one-time tinted card at the top of Profile offers Face ID for next time; the Account group gains a Face ID sign-in switch, and the dashed strip is the unchanged sign-in screen’s QuickType bar offering the passkey.

today.look_for: Two equal cards for one decision: Start (prefilled “Home”, Create live) and Join (code-or-link field, Join disabled), with Sign out underneath; first-run and add-household are the next screens and reuse these cards.

directions.name: Create is the screen, join is a row
directions.look_for: One primary action — the prefilled name, its chips and Create household — and joining demoted to a single chevron row; the dashed block is the TextPrompt that row opens.

directions.name: Share at creation
directions.look_for: First-run is now the invite: “Test Home is ready”, a tile that says you are alone so far, one primary Invite button that opens the share sheet, and a bordered “Just me for now”; the toast is what follows a share.

directions.name: Delete first-run
directions.look_for: Creating the household lands straight on the Add tab; the toast carries the locations footnote first-run used to be a screen for, and the Profile tab wears a one-time badge until an invite is shared.

today.look_for: One inset-grouped scroll, nine headers deep: the invite code with copy/share/⋯ on one row and Share invite link on another, two switches, Learned, Members, Notifications, Plan — the list runs off the bottom, which is the point.

directions.name: Account card + household hub
directions.look_for: The tab collapses to two pushing cards — you (initial, name, email, plan) and your kitchen (Test Home, who is in it) — plus About; everything that used to be a row is one push away, and the footers say what.

directions.name: Flat, three groups, invite as one row
directions.look_for: Still one scroll, but four groups (You · Your household · Preferences · About) and the code, the share link and the active links folded into one “Invite people” row — the sheet it opens is raised over the list.

directions.name: Person here, kitchen on the Pantry tab
directions.look_for: Split frame: the Profile tab keeps only the person (name, bio, plan, reminders), and the Pantry tab’s large title now names the household with a ⋯ menu whose first row is Household settings.

today.look_for: The confirm as it ships: a bottom sheet — “Join Test Home?”, one sentence, Join and a bare Cancel — raised over an empty grey screen with nothing behind it.

directions.name: A landing, not a sheet on grey
directions.look_for: A full-screen invite: tile and “You’re invited to Test Home”, an optional member line, what you will share, which account you are signed in as (with a way to switch), then Join over a bordered Not now.

directions.name: Sheet over the destination
directions.look_for: The same sheet, but raised over the dimmed Pantry tab rather than grey: the app is visible underneath, the sheet gains a tile and a “Signed in as” line, and Cancel stays because the one action commits.

directions.name: Addressed invites with a push
directions.look_for: The invitee’s phone: a push from Ambry (“Test User invited you to Test Home”) lands on the same landing card; the dashed block is the owner’s side — Invite by email, and each person’s Sent/Joined status with Resend.

today.look_for: The gate as it ships: DELETE typed into a field, the button still dimmed until Done commits it, and a keyboard covering a third of the irreversible screen — the cards above have scrolled off under the header.

directions.name: Consequence in the button, Face ID as the gate
directions.look_for: No field, no keyboard: the deleted-things card carries counts from the cache (Test Home — 3 items in 3 locations), the red button says exactly what it will do, and Face ID is the confirmation.

directions.name: Hold to delete
directions.look_for: The same cards, then one red button you hold for two seconds — the darker fill is the progress, caught mid-hold — with the footnote doubling as the VoiceOver hint; no typed word, no keyboard.

directions.name: Grace period
directions.look_for: The safety net shows up at sign-in: a red-tinted card says the account is scheduled for deletion on Sep 19 with Restore account beside Continue deleting; the toast is what the confirm itself now says.

today.look_for: The screen as it ships, at the decided prices: lead paragraph, a benefits card, two radio rows with Yearly preselected and a Save badge, the disclosure, then the CTA, Restore and the two links.

directions.name: One plan, one line
directions.look_for: A single headline about the receipt, three benefit rows, a Monthly | Yearly segment and one big price line — the billed amount is now the loudest object in the body, with the monthly figure in its caption.

directions.name: Comparison card
directions.look_for: A Free | Plus table (scans, ideas, members, photos) sits above the plans, with the hand-entry promise and the household-coverage line as its footer; plans, disclosure and CTA follow as today.

directions.name: Settings card as the sale
directions.look_for: No push: Profile’s Plan group becomes the purchase surface — meter, one benefit line, the price line, the full disclosure, Start free trial, and Restore plus both links crammed inside one grouped card.

today.look_for: The screen as it ships: the figure card, one observation, and a flat dated list of what went off — nothing on it can be acted on, and the figure looks tappable although it is not.

directions.name: Contributors and one fix
directions.look_for: The figure gains a label band (“Good”), and the list is grouped by food with a count — Bananas ×3 is swiped open to its two actions, Remind sooner and Add to list, while Milk is expanded to its dated row.

directions.name: Versus your usual
directions.look_for: Identical to today except one line under the figure — an arrow and “5 points vs August” — which is the whole direction.

directions.name: Month-end moment
directions.look_for: On the 1st a push announces the finished month; the screen gains a This month | Last month segment (Last month selected, showing August) and a Share glyph in the header’s right slot.
